speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing knee pain after recently increasing your physical activity. To help me assess your condition, could you tell me exactly where on the knee the pain is located and what kind of pain it is?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the recent pivoting and twisting during volleyball is a significant clue. Given your age, gender, and the mechanism of injury, could you describe if you hear or feel a "popping" sensation when the pain began, or if you noticed any immediate swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Osgood-Schlatter disease (or apophysitis of the tibial tubercle). The location of pain (medial tibia inferior to patella) combined with a history of recent increased physical activity and weight loss attempts in a young patient is classic for this condition; I will confirm this clinically rather than ordering further imaging.
